description: The family's one Renovate rule set. Every repo in renovate-global.json extends it as github>orangecheck/oc-packages:renovate-family, so a change here reaches all of them on the next run. A repo's own packageRules come after these and win.

packageRules.description: Third-party updates are off: this config tracks the @orangecheck/* family only. Every update type is listed, because a rule naming only patch, minor and major let lockFileMaintenance open third-party PRs that sat for months.

@orangecheck/* patch and minor: one PR per repo on renovate/@orangecheck-(family), one day after the publish. Renovate does not merge it (its token cannot read check runs); the repo's own CI does, in its merge-renovate job, once the gating jobs pass. No PR limit applies to it, so PRs waiting for a person never hold back the one that carries security patches.
@orangecheck/* majors change wire shape: a PR of their own, labelled major-bump, merged by a person, one day after the publish.

Below 1.0 a minor can break (semver promises nothing there, and Renovate marks it breaking). Every such minor in a repo goes into one PR of its own, labelled major-bump, which no merge-renovate job matches: a person reads each CHANGELOG against what the repo imports and merges it. A 0.x patch stays in the family group.

Hold @orangecheck/sdk at 1.18.2, the version each of these sites locks, until the site decodes the reasons the newer minors add: attestation_unread (1.19.0), the signature budget (1.20.0), and chain_unread, utxo_cap_unread and provider_refused_unread (1.21.0). They are minors, so the family rule above would merge them a day after publish, before the site reads them; a bare bump makes attest's report of a capped address worse than today. Each site's decode unit bumps the sdk itself and takes its repo out of this rule: oc-attest-web with A2 (lane-drill), oc-www with its WW-1/WW-2 decode (lane-lock), oc-pledge-web with PL1 (lane-sweep). See lane-sweep/chain-read-failures.md.
